userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

requirements.description: A single stationary, anchored training dummy model (Xtrah962 Training Dummy, assetId 1245720733) stands upright at approximately (0,3,15) in the practice room, providing a fixed hitbox that never moves, retaliates, or resets.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy model is present in the workspace, anchored, upright at ~(0,3,15), with a clear torso/head hitbox reachable from the spawn point, and never changes position or state during play.

requirements.description: Pressing the attack input (left mouse click or bound key) while near the dummy triggers a punch: animation plays, a server-authoritative hit check runs, and on a successful hit the hit sound plays and the on-screen counter increments by one.
requirements.sourceQuote:
The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the attack input near the dummy plays the punch animation, and when the swing connects the hit sound plays and the visible counter increments exactly once per successful swing; missing the dummy produces no sound or counter change.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

requirements.sourceQuote:
The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.

There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.
requirements.acceptance: Rapidly repeating the attack input faster than the animation duration produces at most one counter increment per animation-length interval, verified server-side.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then

		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

plan.reason: Addressing the needs_more_evidence review's concrete defect: the sole embedded script (index 18, Respawn) polls Humanoid.Health every frame and, if it ever drops below 1, clones the dummy, calls the deprecated Instance:makeJoints(), and destroys the original model instance. This clone-and-replace reset directly conflicts with target_dummy's acceptance criterion that the dummy 'never changes position or state' and has 'no fail state, health system, or win condition,' and it is unsafe/legacy behavior (makeJoints, unbounded polling loop) that should not be carried into the final place. Since this design has no damage mechanic that would ever lower the dummy's Health, the script serves no required gameplay purpose and is removed outright rather than stubbed, per the instruction that inert stubs do not resolve defects — removal eliminates the conflicting behavior cleanly while keeping every other part of the hierarchy intact. All reusable static content (Head/Torso parts, SpecialMesh geometry, the Torso Decal, and the Humanoid) is preserved untouched so it remains available as the stationary hitbox for later touch/proximity hit detection. Anchoring, exact (0,3,15) placement, Decal texture rendering verification, and wiring to the separately-owned hit_sound/hit_counter_ui components are explicitly deferred to the dummy_placement and downstream integration tasks, not fabricated here.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

requirements.description: A single stationary, anchored training dummy model (Xtrah962 Training Dummy, assetId 1245720733) stands upright at approximately (0,3,15) in the practice room, providing a fixed hitbox that never moves, retaliates, or resets.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy model is present in the workspace, anchored, upright at ~(0,3,15), with a clear torso/head hitbox reachable from the spawn point, and never changes position or state during play.

requirements.description: Pressing the attack input (left mouse click or bound key) while near the dummy triggers a punch: animation plays, a server-authoritative hit check runs, and on a successful hit the hit sound plays and the on-screen counter increments by one.
requirements.sourceQuote:
The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the attack input near the dummy plays the punch animation, and when the swing connects the hit sound plays and the visible counter increments exactly once per successful swing; missing the dummy produces no sound or counter change.

requirements.description: The practice room and dummy read as a gritty gym/dojo training space: matte gray dummy coloring, mat-textured floor, simple walls, and even lighting, avoiding fantasy/sci-fi framing.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

plan.reason: Addressing the needs_more_evidence review's concrete defect: the sole embedded script (index 18, Respawn) polls Humanoid.Health every frame and, if it ever drops below 1, clones the dummy, calls the deprecated Instance:makeJoints(), and destroys the original model instance. inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
