requirements.sourceQuote:
A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one ~20x20 stud room with walkable anchored floor, boundary walls, a SpawnLocation near the center oriented toward the dummy, and lighting sufficient to clearly see the dummy and UI.

requirements.description: Each player's hit counter and cooldown state is tracked independently by UserId on the server, reset appropriately on join, cleaned up on leave, and the HUD/animation bindings rebind correctly after a character respawn without duplicating UI or losing the visible count.
requirements.acceptance: Two simultaneous players see independent counters that do not interfere with each other; a player's counter/cooldown state is removed from server memory on leave; after respawning, the HUD shows exactly one counter label continuing to track hits correctly.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.

need.role: Stationary target the player punches to test timing and trigger the hit counter.

intent.experienceRole: Serves as the practice target players repeatedly punch to test their combat timing and trigger scoring feedback, anchoring the entire gameplay loop.

reusableFeatures: Existing humanoid rig or part layout usable as a hitbox for touch detection

Anchored base plate or stand geometry included with the model

need.role: Plays on the player character when the attack input is pressed, giving the punch visual weight.
need.constraints: R15-compatible single-arm jab or straight punch animation, non-looping, duration approximately 0.3-0.6 seconds, playable via AnimationController/Animator on the default player rig, timed to roughly align with hit registration.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the visual feedback of the player's attack action, making punches feel physical and readable so hits feel earned.
intent.interaction: Triggered the instant the player presses the attack input; plays once on the player's arm/torso during the punch swing, timed to align with hit detection on the dummy and the accompanying hit sound.
reusableFeatures: Any existing attack/punch animations already rigged to the player character

need.role: Audible confirmation that a punch has successfully landed on the dummy.

intent.experienceRole: Delivers audible feedback confirming a successful punch connects with the dummy, reinforcing the hit counter increment and making hits feel satisfying.
intent.interaction: Plays once, immediately, whenever a punch registers as a hit on the dummy. Purely reactive audio feedback; the player does not directly control the sound.
reusableFeatures: Any existing combat or impact sound cues bundled with the dummy model

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.

requirements.description: The server authoritatively validates each punch attempt against the dummy's hitbox using a short-range touch/proximity or raycast check plus a distance check, rejecting hits that are out of range or spoofed by the client.
requirements.acceptance: Server logs/tests show punch requests from beyond melee range or without a valid swing are rejected and do not increment any player's counter, while in-range swings are accepted.

requirements.description: A per-player cooldown equal to the punch animation's duration is enforced so a single swing cannot register multiple hits or be spammed faster than the animation allows.
requirements.sourceQuote:
The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.
requirements.acceptance: Rapidly repeating the attack input faster than the animation duration produces at most one counter increment per animation-length interval, verified server-side.

requirements.description: A single enclosed practice room roughly 20x20 studs with a flat, mat-textured floor, simple boundary walls, a safe collidable spawn near the center facing the dummy, and even baseplate-style lighting.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one ~20x20 stud room with walkable anchored floor, boundary walls, a SpawnLocation near the center oriented toward the dummy, and lighting sufficient to clearly see the dummy and UI.

requirements.description: Each player's hit counter and cooldown state is tracked independently by UserId on the server, reset appropriately on join, cleaned up on leave, and the HUD/animation bindings rebind correctly after a character respawn without duplicating UI or losing the visible count.
requirements.acceptance: Two simultaneous players see independent counters that do not interfere with each other; a player's counter/cooldown state is removed from server memory on leave; after respawning, the HUD shows exactly one counter label continuing to track hits correctly.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Gritty, approachable gym/dojo training-space aesthetic rather than fantasy or sci-fi. Matte gray/neutral color palette: a mat-textured (or mat-colored) flat floor, simple flat walls or boundary markers, even functional lighting with no dramatic shadows or skybox complexity. The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

data.reason: Dummy geometry/mesh/Humanoid/Decal are reusable as a static hitbox, but the sole embedded script (Respawn) implements a clone-and-replace reset tied to Humanoid.Health that directly conflicts with the requirement that the dummy 'never resets.' It must be reviewed/disabled before integration. No placement/Anchored evidence yet, and hit_sound/hit_counter_ui are not provided by this asset.

serializedMedia.purpose: Decal texture applied to the dummy's Torso part, contributing to its tape-wrapped/gym visual appearance; unverified for availability or rendering.

sources.behavior: Infinite loop (wait(0)) polls script.Parent.Humanoid.Health each frame; when Health<1, waits 1s, clones the dummy model captured at script start, parents the clone into the original model's parent, calls deprecated Instance:makeJoints(), then removes (destroys) the original dummy model instance, effectively respawning a fresh dummy clone in place of the 'defeated' one.

requirements.reason: Model supplies Head/Torso/parts/Humanoid/Decal usable as a stationary hitbox, but evidence shows no Anchored/CFrame placement at (0,3,15), and the embedded Respawn script would clone-and-replace the dummy if Humanoid.Health ever drops below 1, conflicting with the 'never resets' acceptance criterion. Placement and disabling/removing this script are outstanding integration work.

This component contains no Sound instances or audio references; the impact sound must come from the separately selected hit-sound asset and be wired to a server-confirmed hit event, which is not part of this dummy's static content.
This component contains no ScreenGui/UI elements; the persistent hit counter must be authored separately (HitCounterHUD task) and is unrelated to the dummy model's own hierarchy or scripts.

integrationNotes: The Respawn script's clone/destroy behavior on Humanoid.Health<1 must be disabled or removed prior to placement, since the design requires the dummy to never reset or change state, even though nothing in the current design deals damage to trigger it.
Anchored state and exact world position (~0,3,15) for the dummy are not established by this evidence; verify/set these during the dummy_placement task.

hit_sound and hit_counter_ui requirements are satisfied by other pending components (hitSound asset, HitCounterHUD script), not by this dummy asset; no substitute sound/UI should be authored inside this component.
Decal Texture rbxassetid://406436910 on Torso is unverified content (availability/rights/appearance not confirmed) and should be checked during dummy_placement.

need.role: Stationary target the player punches to test timing and trigger the hit counter.
need.constraints: Humanoid-shaped stationary practice dummy, roughly 5-6 studs tall, matte gym/gray color scheme, anchored base or stand, R15-compatible rig acceptable but no locomotion needed, no moving parts required, must have a clear torso/head hitbox for touch or proximity hit detection.

intent.experienceRole: Serves as the practice target players repeatedly punch to test their combat timing and trigger scoring feedback, anchoring the entire gameplay loop.
intent.interaction: Player approaches and presses the attack input to swing at the dummy; on a successful hit the game plays the hit sound and immediately increments the on-screen hit counter. The dummy itself does not move, attack back, or reset.
reusableFeatures: Existing humanoid rig or part layout usable as a hitbox for touch detection
Any built-in idle or wobble animation already on the dummy model
Anchored base plate or stand geometry included with the model

need.role: Plays on the player character when the attack input is pressed, giving the punch visual weight.
need.constraints: R15-compatible single-arm jab or straight punch animation, non-looping, duration approximately 0.3-0.6 seconds, playable via AnimationController/Animator on the default player rig, timed to roughly align with hit registration.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the visual feedback of the player's attack action, making punches feel physical and readable so hits feel earned.
intent.interaction: Triggered the instant the player presses the attack input; plays once on the player's arm/torso during the punch swing, timed to align with hit detection on the dummy and the accompanying hit sound.
reusableFeatures: Any existing attack/punch animations already rigged to the player character
Default Roblox R15 upper-body animation slots

need.role: Audible confirmation that a punch has successfully landed on the dummy.
need.constraints: Short percussive punch/impact sound effect, 0.2-0.5 seconds duration, non-looping, clear and punchy for melee combat feedback, no music or dialogue.

intent.experienceRole: Delivers audible feedback confirming a successful punch connects with the dummy, reinforcing the hit counter increment and making hits feel satisfying.
intent.interaction: Plays once, immediately, whenever a punch registers as a hit on the dummy. Purely reactive audio feedback; the player does not directly control the sound.
reusableFeatures: Any existing combat or impact sound cues bundled with the dummy model
Default Roblox damage/hit sound effects

plan.reason: Addressing the needs_more_evidence review's concrete defect: the sole embedded script (index 18, Respawn) polls Humanoid.Health every frame and, if it ever drops below 1, clones the dummy, calls the deprecated Instance:makeJoints(), and destroys the original model instance. This clone-and-replace reset directly conflicts with target_dummy's acceptance criterion that the dummy 'never changes position or state' and has 'no fail state, health system, or win condition,' and it is unsafe/legacy behavior (makeJoints, unbounded polling loop) that should not be carried into the final place. Since this design has no damage mechanic that would ever lower the dummy's Health, the script serves no required gameplay purpose and is removed outright rather than stubbed, per the instruction that inert stubs do not resolve defects — removal eliminates the conflicting behavior cleanly while keeping every other part of the hierarchy intact. All reusable static content (Head/Torso parts, SpecialMesh geometry, the Torso Decal, and the Humanoid) is preserved untouched so it remains available as the stationary hitbox for later touch/proximity hit detection. Anchoring, exact (0,3,15) placement, Decal texture rendering verification, and wiring to the separately-owned hit_sound/hit_counter_ui components are explicitly deferred to the dummy_placement and downstream integration tasks, not fabricated here.

removeSubtrees.reason: Removes the Respawn Script whose Humanoid.Health<1 clone/destroy loop (using deprecated Instance:makeJoints()) conflicts with the requirement that the dummy never resets, retaliates, or changes state; no damage system exists in this design to justify retaining this reset behavior, and stubbing it in place would leave dead/unsafe code rather than resolving the defect.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.

The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

requirements.description: The server authoritatively validates each punch attempt against the dummy's hitbox using a short-range touch/proximity or raycast check plus a distance check, rejecting hits that are out of range or spoofed by the client.
requirements.acceptance: Server logs/tests show punch requests from beyond melee range or without a valid swing are rejected and do not increment any player's counter, while in-range swings are accepted.

requirements.description: A per-player cooldown equal to the punch animation's duration is enforced so a single swing cannot register multiple hits or be spammed faster than the animation allows.
requirements.sourceQuote:
The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.
requirements.acceptance: Rapidly repeating the attack input faster than the animation duration produces at most one counter increment per animation-length interval, verified server-side.

requirements.description: A single enclosed practice room roughly 20x20 studs with a flat, mat-textured floor, simple boundary walls, a safe collidable spawn near the center facing the dummy, and even baseplate-style lighting.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one ~20x20 stud room with walkable anchored floor, boundary walls, a SpawnLocation near the center oriented toward the dummy, and lighting sufficient to clearly see the dummy and UI.

requirements.description: Each player's hit counter and cooldown state is tracked independently by UserId on the server, reset appropriately on join, cleaned up on leave, and the HUD/animation bindings rebind correctly after a character respawn without duplicating UI or losing the visible count.
requirements.acceptance: Two simultaneous players see independent counters that do not interfere with each other; a player's counter/cooldown state is removed from server memory on leave; after respawning, the HUD shows exactly one counter label continuing to track hits correctly.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. playerExperience.assetStrategy: All three approved assets are treated as complete reusable Marketplace components, not raw geometry to rebuild. The Training Dummy (1245720733) is expected to supply the standing hitbox and pose directly; it reports one embedded script, so inspection must review that script before trusting any embedded behavior — only missing integration (server hit validation, sound/counter hookup) will be authored, and any unsafe or unsupported script content will be reported as a review gap rather than silently replaced. The R15 Punching Animations model (12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) is a raw KeyframeSequence source per the animation capability contract: it is usable for Studio playback via RegisterKeyframeSequence assigned to Animation.AnimationId and played through the player's Animator, with publishing remaining a recorded, non-blocking limitation — no procedural tween substitute will be authored in its place. The impact sound (126976659766267) is a verified Marketplace Audio asset that must pass load/playback/listening checks before being wired to the server-confirmed hit event; no builtin or generated sound will be substituted if it fails. Missing integration to author: RemoteEvent plumbing between client input and server validation, server-side distance/cooldown/hit checks against the dummy's hitbox, sound playback triggered from server-confirmed hits, and a persistent per-player HUD counter — none of which is expected to be supplied by the assets themselves.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Combat Trainer
playerExperience.summary: A single-room boxing/dojo practice trainer. On spawn the player stands in a compact ~20x20 stud mat-floored room, facing a stationary training dummy anchored a few studs away at (0,3,15); a hit counter reads '0' in the top-right corner. Walking into melee range and pressing the attack input (left click or bound key) plays a punch animation on the player's arm; the server checks range/aim against the dummy's hitbox, and on a confirmed hit the impact sound plays at the dummy and the counter increments by one, giving the player an immediate, repeatable feedback loop of approach-punch-hear/see-count. A short per-swing cooldown matching the animation length stops duplicate hits from one press. There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb. Assumptions applied without further questions: default R15 character with no custom rig, single mouse/keybind attack with no combos, per-player session-only counter with no leaderboard, exactly one dummy with no spawning/respawning, and standard baseplate-style lighting/materials for the gym-style room.

The dummy is the visual focal point directly ahead of spawn, tape-wrapped/matte in tone, standing upright on a small anchored base. The HUD counter is a clean, legible numeric label fixed to the top-right corner, high-contrast against the room so it reads at a glance during rapid punching. Punch feedback should be readable: animation swing, synced impact sound at the dummy, and an immediate counter tick, reinforcing a satisfying but minimal training-room loop.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

The player controls a standard Roblox character standing near a single stationary target dummy. Pressing an attack input (default: left mouse click or a designated key) triggers a punch: the player's punch animation plays, and a hit check determines whether the punch connects with the dummy's hitbox (via touch detection or a short-range proximity/raycast check in front of the player). If the punch connects, the hit sound plays immediately, and an on-screen numeric counter increments by one. The counter is displayed persistently in a corner of the screen throughout play. The dummy is fully stationary and non-aggressive: it does not move, retaliate, take damage state changes, or reset, and there is no fail state, health system, or win condition beyond accumulating hits. The loop is a simple, repeatable practice cycle: approach, punch, hear/see feedback, watch the counter climb. A short cooldown between successive punches (e.g., matching the punch animation length) prevents input spam from firing multiple hits per single swing.
The player uses the default Roblox R15 humanoid character with no custom rig requirements.
The attack input is a simple, single keybind or mouse click with no combo or charge system.
Hit detection uses a short-range touch or proximity check between the player's punching hand/arm and the dummy's hitbox.
The on-screen counter is a basic UI label with no persistence across sessions and no leaderboard integration.
There is exactly one target dummy in the world; no spawning, respawning, or multiple targets are required.
A brief per-punch cooldown equal to the animation duration prevents duplicate hit registration from a single swing.

A minimal, arcade-style fighting/training theme centered on a boxing or martial-arts practice space. The tone is casual and skill-focused rather than narrative-driven: the player is a fighter honing technique against a static training dummy, similar to a gym heavy-bag station. Visual and audio style leans toward gritty, energetic combat-sport aesthetics (gym mats, tape-wrapped dummy, punchy impact sound) rather than fantasy or sci-fi framing, keeping the experience approachable and immediately understandable.
The setting is a realistic-leaning gym/dojo training theme rather than a fantasy or sci-fi combat theme.
No opponent AI, story, or progression narrative is implied beyond simple practice against a dummy.
Color palette and materials should read as a training facility (mats, tape, matte dummy) rather than an ornate arena.

A single small enclosed room or platform serving as a practice arena, roughly 20x20 studs, with a flat floor (mat-textured if available) and simple walls or boundary markers to keep the player near the dummy. The player spawns near the center of the room, facing the target dummy which is anchored a few studs away at approximately (0, 3, 15) so it stands upright on the floor. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed corner of the screen (e.g., top-right) and remains visible at all times during play. Lighting is simple and even, sufficient to clearly see the dummy and read punch feedback; no complex weather, day/night cycle, or multi-room layout is needed. The space is intentionally compact and free of obstacles so the punch-and-feedback loop remains uninterrupted.
A single-room practice arena is sufficient; no multi-level or outdoor environment is required.
The dummy's fixed position near the room center is adequate for consistent hit-range access.
Standard baseplate-style lighting and materials are acceptable; no custom skybox or weather system is needed.
The UI counter sits in a fixed screen corner and does not need to be repositioned dynamically.

There is no health, retaliation, win condition, or persistence beyond the session — the goal is simply to watch the counter climb.
